1.name: Main gear leg
1.spec: Tapered flat spring, 90×30 at the saddle to 60×18 at the tip
1.note: The spring itself: a beam that bends about 59 mm at the axle under the static load. Its taper keeps the bending stress nearly even along it.

2.name: Saddle forging
2.spec: Outboard fitting, at the fuselage's lower corner
2.note: Sits on top of the leg where it leaves the fuselage and presses it down: it carries the wheel load plus the inboard bolt's pull, about 5 times the load.

3.name: Saddle cap
3.note: Closes the saddle under the leg, so the leg is held both ways, up in a landing and down when the wheel hangs in flight.

4.name: Cap bolt
4.note: Pull the cap up against the saddle either side of the leg (fore and aft of it), clamping the leg between them.

5.name: Inboard fitting
5.spec: Block on the gear box bulkheads
5.note: Holds the leg's inner end up. The leg is a lever on the saddle: the wheel pushes its outer end up, so its inner end pushes down here.

6.name: Inboard bolt
6.note: Through the leg's inner end and the fitting: it locates the leg and stops it sliding out sideways or lifting off the fitting.

7.name: Gear box bulkhead
7.spec: Two webs, fore and aft of the leg
7.note: The fuselage frames either side of the leg that the saddle and the inboard fitting bolt to; they spread the landing loads into the skin.

8.name: Cabin floor and seat rails
8.spec: 1.0 mm sheet on the bulkheads, two rails per seat
8.note: The floor over the gear box, with the seats' rails on it: the people ride directly above the legs' fittings.

9.name: Skin, belly and side
9.spec: With a slot for the leg
9.note: The fuselage's lower shell. The leg passes out through a slot at the corner, which is why the saddle sits right there.

10.name: Axle
10.spec: Ø31.75 hollow spindle, forged with its mounting block, and a spacer
10.note: Bolted under the leg's tip; the wheel turns on it on two bearings. The spacer sets the inner bearing's place against the torque plate.

11.name: Axle bolt and tapered shim
11.note: Bolt the axle block to the leg. The tapered shim tilts the axle so the wheel stands upright at the static load, not in flight.

12.name: Torque plate
12.spec: Keyed on the axle, with two anchor bushings
12.note: The brake's anchor: the caliper hangs on its two bushings and the braking torque goes through it into the axle and the leg.

13.name: Wheel
13.spec: 6.00-6, two halves split at the centre
13.note: Two halves bolted together so the tyre can be fitted without levering it over a rim. The inner half's four lugs carry the disc.

14.name: Wheel tie bolt
14.note: Join the two halves and clamp the brake disc to the inner one, so the disc turns with the wheel and its torque reaches the tyre.

15.name: Tapered roller bearing
15.note: One each side of the hub, facing apart, so together they carry the wheel's load and the side loads of a turn or a scrubbing landing.

16.name: Grease seal
16.note: Keep the bearings' grease in and the runway's grit and water out.

17.name: Axle nut
17.note: Sets the bearings' preload: tightened until the wheel just drags, backed off to the next slot and pinned.

18.name: Tyre and inner tube
18.note: The first spring, about 26 mm of squash under the static load; when the track widens on landing it scrubs sideways, which is the gear's only real damping.

19.name: Brake disc
19.note: Turns with the wheel between the two linings. Clamped at 30 bar it makes about 300 N·m of torque at its 79 mm lining radius.

20.name: Caliper cylinder
20.spec: One Ø44.45 bore, floating on two anchor bolts
20.note: Line pressure in its bore pushes the piston out; the reaction slides the whole caliper back, pulling the back plate in, so both linings clamp alike.

21.name: Caliper piston
21.note: The receiving end of Pascal: 1552 mm² against the master cylinder's 127 mm², so the clamp force is 12 times the rod force.

22.name: Pressure plate and lining
22.note: Pushed by the piston onto the disc's inner face. Each lining's friction is about 0.4 of its clamp force.

23.name: Back plate and lining
23.note: Pulled onto the disc's outer face as the floating caliper slides back: the second friction face, so the torque is 2μN·r.

24.name: Anchor bolt
24.spec: Two, sliding in the torque plate
24.note: Tie the cylinder to the back plate around the disc's rim and slide in the torque plate's bushings, which take the braking torque.

25.name: Brake line and hose
25.spec: Ø4.76 tube along the leg, flexible hose to the caliper
25.note: The column of fluid between toe and wheel. The hose takes the leg's bending and the caliper's float.

26.name: Master cylinder and reservoir
26.note: At rest its bore is open to the reservoir through a tiny compensating port; the piston's cup covers it after 1.6 mm, and from then on the toe makes pressure.

27.name: Piston, cup and rod
27.spec: Ø12.7, with its cup and O-ring
27.note: The sending end of Pascal: the rod force over the bore's 127 mm² is the line pressure, about 30 bar for a firm toe.

28.name: Return spring
28.note: Pushes the piston back when the toe lifts, so the cup clears the port and the line falls back to the reservoir's pressure.

29.name: Toe brake pedal
29.spec: Hinged at its foot, 130 mm to the toe, 52 mm to the rod
29.note: The upper part of each rudder pedal: pressing with the toe tips it forward, a 2.5 to 1 lever onto the master cylinder's rod.
